dialect.detail: Student exercise targeting GnuCOBOL or similar PC-based compiler (IBM-PC declared in SOURCE/OBJECT-COMPUTER). Portuguese-language identifiers and Brazilian context. Uses VALUE OF FILE-ID clause typical of older PC COBOL dialects.
evidence: LABEL RECORD IS OMMITED (misspelling common in student code)

purpose.domain_detail: FATEC-SP (Faculdade de Tecnologia de São Paulo) student exercise for a tourism company (TURISMAR TURISMOS) customer registration validation system
purpose.summary: Reads customer records from CADCLI.DAT, validates CPF (Brazilian tax ID using check-digit algorithm), name, Brazilian state code, city, and email fields. Valid records are written to CADOK.DAT; invalid records are printed to a report (RELOCOR) listing which fields failed validation.

notable_features: CPF (Brazilian tax ID) check-digit validation algorithm using OCCURS and iterative COMPUTE
88-level condition for all 27 Brazilian state codes (ESTADO-VALIDO)
VALUE OF FILE-ID clause for file assignment
WRITE ... AFTER ADVANCING PAGE/LINE for report formatting
Multi-level header printing with page overflow control (CT-LIN)
verdict.notes: Author is Fabio Costa, institution FATEC-SP, dated 13/10/2015. The misspelling 'OMMITED' instead of 'OMITTED' in the RELOCOR FD is a common student error. No COPY statements or CALLs; self-contained single program. CPF validation logic resets CTR1/CTR2 between SOMA1 and SOMA2 loops but does not reinitialize CPF-SOMA1/CPF-SOMA2 between records, which is a likely bug in the student code.
